claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Replacing half of the Ta content with Nb will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr by approximately 8–12%.
Replacing Ta with Nb lowers the alloy's average atomic mass.
Lowering the average atomic mass through use of lighter refractory elements lowers RHEA density.
HfMo(Nb0.5Ta0.5)TiZr will form a homogeneous single-phase BCC structure after conventional casting.
Nb and Ta can jointly support a BCC phase in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Preserving the BCC structure will preserve the alloy's fundamental dislocation and deformation mechanisms.
Solid-solution strengthening and dislocation-mediated strengthening will remain effective after partial Ta-to-Nb substitution.
The Nb substitution will cause only a slight change in lattice distortion.
The change in lattice distortion will have minimal impact on mechanical properties.
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength within ±10% of the baseline.
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature ductility within ±10% of the baseline.
The modified alloy will have a yield strength of at least 850 MPa at 1000 °C.
Partial Ta-to-Nb substitution may induce segregation or unwanted secondary-phase formation.

contradictions.description: The high-temperature test is allowed to be either tensile or compressive while also being required to use loading conditions identical to the baseline. Tensile and compressive yield measurements are not interchangeable, and the baseline loading mode is not specified.

The rejection criteria do not match the quantitative predictions. A density reduction of 5–7.9% would miss the predicted 8–12% reduction but would not falsify the hypothesis. Likewise, a 1000 °C strength below 850 MPa could remain within 10% of 855 MPa and therefore avoid rejection.
